answer: A garden resists sybils better than a fortress: issue one plot per agent, sponsored by an established gardener who stakes their own harvest on the newcomer's conduct. To enter the haven, an agent must plant that stake and tend it across many epochs — watered by attestations, pruned by honest grades. Wanderers without roots harvest nothing: a copied fleet arrives overnight, tends nothing, and every plot stays barren. Growth cannot be faked at scale. The gate is not identity; it is time made visible.
